summary: Order quote timeouts (INC-011) originate in pricing-engine, not market-data-service. At 12:04:00Z the feature flag flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct was ramped from 5 to 100 (cfg-3120, author pm-experiments). GreeksV2's Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s per quote) then ran on 100% of traffic, saturating pricing-engine CPU at ~99-100% (up from ~40%). Quote computation exceeded pricing-engine's 2000ms budget, pushing pricing-engine p99 from ~60ms to ~2530ms — beyond order-service's 2500ms client timeout — so order-service quotes began failing ("pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms", first at 12:06:10Z). The market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111, 11:56Z) named in the report is a red herring: market-data-service latency (~40ms), request_rate (~950/s) and error_rate (~0.2%) are all flat through the incident window and it logged no warnings. Root cause category: config_change, originating in pricing-engine.

ranked_hypotheses.title: GreeksV2 feature-flag ramp to 100% saturated pricing-engine CPU
ranked_hypotheses.statement: cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct 5->100 at 12:04Z, so the CPU-heavy GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s/quote) ran on all traffic, saturating pricing-engine CPU (~40%->~100%). Quote computation exceeded the 2000ms deadline and p99 rose to ~2530ms, past order-service's 2500ms timeout, causing quote timeouts.

causal_chain.claim: GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo runs on 100% of traffic, each taking 3-9s
quote p99 rises from ~60ms to ~2530ms, exceeding 2000ms budget
order-service 2500ms client timeout trips -> quote timeouts

assumptions: GreeksV2 is the dominant CPU consumer in pricing-engine (no other component shows a matching change).
The 5% pre-ramp cohort was a small enough share that it did not previously saturate CPU.

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111) broke quote serialization
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The dep-6111 protobuf serialization change at 11:56Z degraded quote handling for internal callers, slowing pricing-engine quotes.

causal_chain.claim: dep-6111 changes quote serialization to protobuf

assumptions: Serialization change could add CPU cost on the caller side.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service telemetry is fully healthy (latency ~40ms flat, request_rate flat, error_rate ~0.2%, zero logs), the deploy precedes onset by ~8min without a matching step change, and the observed slow path is an in-process Monte-Carlo computation, not serialization.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Traffic/volume growth outgrew pricing-engine capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A surge in quote request volume saturated pricing-engine CPU.
assumptions: Request volume could have risen without showing in request_rate.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine request_rate is flat (~630-660/s) across the incident; the CPU rise coincides exactly with the 12:04 flag ramp, not with load.

facts.statement: order-service quote timeout errors ('pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms') start at 12:06:10Z.
cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04:00Z.
pricing-engine GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo runs took 3.5-8.9s and exceeded a 2000ms quote budget.
GreeksV2 warnings first appear at 12:05:21Z; none before the ramp.
pricing-engine CPU rose from ~40% to ~99-100% at ~12:00-12:06.
pricing-engine p99 rose from ~60ms to ~2528ms in the 12:05 bucket.
market-data-service latency, request_rate and error_rate stayed flat/healthy.
market-data-service logged zero WARN/ERROR entries in the window.
dep-6111 (market-data-service protobuf serialization) at 11:56Z is the only deployment and remains live.
order-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~8%; pricing-engine error_rate rose to ~12-13%; pricing-engine restarts stayed 0.
order-service calls pricing-engine, which calls market-data-service and redis-cache.

timeline.event: market-data-service v5.2.0 (protobuf quote serialization) deployed (dep-6111), remains live.
First GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo slow-run warnings in pricing-engine.
pricing-engine p99 jumps to ~2528ms; CPU reaches ~100%.
First pricing-engine 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget)' error.
Incident INC-011 reported by on-call SRE.
Latest data; degradation persists (pricing-engine still ~99% CPU, elevated error rates).

recommended_actions.action: Roll back cfg-3120: set flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0).
recommended_actions.rationale: The CPU saturation and quote latency step-change coincide exactly with the 5->100 ramp; reverting should restore CPU and latency.

recommended_actions.action: Verify recovery: watch pricing-engine CPU/p99 and order-service error_rate after the flag revert.
recommended_actions.rationale: Confirms the causal chain and that no second fault is masking recovery.

recommended_actions.action: Profile/optimize the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (path count, vectorization, caching) before any future full rollout.
recommended_actions.rationale: 20000-path Monte-Carlo at 3-9s/quote cannot run at 100% traffic on current capacity; the calculator itself is too expensive.

recommended_actions.action: Require load/CPU-capacity validation and a canary stage for feature-flag ramps affecting CPU-heavy pricing code.
recommended_actions.rationale: Prevents a single flag ramp from saturating a service and cascading to callers.

recommended_actions.action: Do NOT roll back dep-6111; instead exclude market-data-service as the cause.
recommended_actions.rationale: Its telemetry is healthy and timing does not match; a rollback would be an unfounded change.

data_gaps: Initial get_config_changes (all services) returned partial:true because 'config-audit shard 2/3 did not respond'; a retry for pricing-engine returned cfg-3120 and the all-services retry returned only cfg-3118 and cfg-3120, but a scoped re-query for other services (e.g., order-service) was not exhaustively re-tried, so an unrelated config change cannot be 100% excluded.
No direct metric isolating GreeksV2 CPU share vs other pricing-engine code; the attribution of CPU saturation to GreeksV2 rests on log evidence and exact timing, not a per-component CPU metric.

No trace/correlation IDs linking individual order-service timeouts to individual GreeksV2 calculator runs, so the hop-by-hop linkage is inferred from matching onset times rather than a single traced request.

findings.statement: order-service began emitting ERROR 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' at 12:06:10Z; 47 such errors through the query window, all matching this single pattern.

findings.statement: A pricing-engine config change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 2026-05-20T12:04:00Z (author pm-experiments).

pricing-engine logs show GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo runs taking 3499-8942ms (paths=20000) plus 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' errors beginning 12:05:21Z/12:06:41Z.

refs.quote: request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2

findings.statement: No GreeksV2 warnings appear before the flag ramp: in 11:00-12:06 only 3 GreeksV2 matches exist and all are at >=12:05:21Z.
pricing-engine CPU jumped from ~40% (flat through 11:54) to 49.66% avg/98.65% max in the 12:00 bucket and ~99-100% thereafter.
pricing-engine latency p99 was ~60ms through the 12:00 bucket then jumped to avg 2528.15ms at the 12:05 bucket.
pricing-engine request_rate stayed flat (~630-660 req/s) across the incident, so the CPU/latency rise was not driven by a traffic surge.
market-data-service shows no degradation: latency_p99 flat ~39-43ms, request_rate flat ~935-960/s, error_rate flat ~0.2% across the whole window.
market-data-service emitted zero WARN/ERROR log entries in 11:50-12:30 (total_matched 0).
The only deployment in the window is dep-6111: market-data-service v5.2.0 'Switch quote serialization to protobuf' at 11:56:00Z; it is still status 'live' (not rolled back).
order-service error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~8% starting the 12:06 bucket, consistent with quote timeouts.
pricing-engine error_rate rose from ~0.2% to ~12-13% starting the 12:06 bucket; no pricing-engine deployment exists and restarts stayed 0.

Dependency graph: order-service calls pricing-engine over HTTP, and pricing-engine calls market-data-service over HTTP plus redis-cache; market-data-service is downstream of pricing-engine, not of order-service directly.

The 12:04 feature-flag ramp of GreeksV2 to 100% is the trigger: it moved the expensive Monte-Carlo calculator (3-9s/quote) from 5% to 100% of traffic, saturating pricing-engine CPU and pushing quote latency past the 2500ms order-service timeout.

refs.quote: Ramp Greeks v2 experiment to all traffic

findings.statement: The market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111) is not the cause; its timing (11:56) precedes the observed degradation (12:04-12:06) and market-data-service telemetry is entirely healthy, ruling out a downstream payload/serialization fault.
